title.zh: 卷一百九十五 列傳第八十三 王守仁
title.raw: 卷一百九十五 列傳第八十三 王守仁 Volume 195 Biographies 83: Wang Shouren

sentences.zh: 王守仁附:冀元亨

translations.literal: Wang Shouren, with appendix: Ji Yuanheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, with appended biography: Ji Yuanheng

sentences.zh: 王守仁

translations.literal: Wang Shouren
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren

sentences.zh: 王守仁，字伯安，余姚人。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren, courtesy name Bo'an, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, whose courtesy name was Bo'an, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 父華，字德輝，成化十七年進士第一。

translations.literal: His father Hua, courtesy name Dehui, ranked first among jinshi graduates in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Hua, styled Dehui, had placed first on the jinshi examination in Chenghua 17 (1481).

sentences.zh: 授修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician-Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 弘治中 ，累官學士、少詹事。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign he successively held the posts of Academician and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi he rose through the ranks to Academician and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 華有器度，在講幄最久，孝宗甚眷之。

translations.literal: Hua had breadth of bearing; he served longest in the imperial lecture hall, and Emperor Xiaozong favored him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was a man of stature and had lectured in the imperial study longer than anyone; Emperor Xiaozong held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 李廣貴幸，華講《大學衍義》，至唐李輔國與張後表裡用事，指陳甚切。

translations.literal: When Li Guang enjoyed imperial favor, Hua lectured on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; reaching the passage on Tang Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang acting in concert from within and without, his pointed commentary was very trenchant.
translations.idiomatic: While the favored eunuch Li Guang was in power, Hua was expounding the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; when he came to the Tang episode of Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang manipulating affairs from inside and outside the palace, his pointed remarks were cutting indeed.

sentences.zh: 帝命中官賜食勞焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a eunuch to bestow food upon him as a reward for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch with food to reward him for his effort.

sentences.zh: 正德初，進禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhengde reign he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengde he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以守仁忤劉瑾，出為南京吏部尚書，坐事罷。

translations.literal: Because Shouren had offended Liu Jin, he was transferred out to be Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, then dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren ran afoul of Liu Jin, Hua was sent out as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing and soon dismissed on a charge.

sentences.zh: 旋以《會典》小誤，降右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after, for a minor error in the Collected Statutes, he was demoted to Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was shortly demoted to Right Vice Minister over a small mistake in the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，乃復故，無何卒。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he was restored to his former rank, but before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's downfall he was restored to his old post, but died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 華性孝，母岑年逾百歲卒。

translations.literal: Hua was by nature filial; his mother Cen died when she was over a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was deeply filial; his mother Lady Cen died at more than a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 華已年七十余，猶寢苫蔬食，士論多之。

translations.literal: Though Hua himself was already over seventy, he still slept on mourning mats and ate plain food; men of learning greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hua himself was past seventy, he still slept on a mourning mat and ate only plain food, and scholars widely commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 守仁娠十四月而生。

translations.literal: Shouren was carried in the womb for fourteen months before he was born.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was in the womb fourteen months before he was born.

sentences.zh: 祖母夢神人自雲中送兒下，因名雲。

translations.literal: His grandmother dreamed that a divine man descended from the clouds bringing a child, so they named him Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother dreamed of a divine being descending from the clouds with a child, and for that reason he was first named Yun.

sentences.zh: 五歲不能言，異人拊之，更名守仁，乃言。

translations.literal: At five he could not speak; a stranger clapped him on the back, he was renamed Shouren, and then he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Until he was five he could not speak; a stranger patted his head, he was renamed Shouren, and only then did he begin to talk.

sentences.zh: 年十五 ，訪客居庸、山海關。

translations.literal: At fifteen he traveled as a guest to Juyong and Shanhai Passes.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he visited as a traveler the passes at Juyong and Shanhai.

sentences.zh: 時闌出塞，縱觀山川形勝。

translations.literal: At times he slipped past the frontier posts to survey broadly the terrain and strategic features of the mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He would sometimes slip beyond the frontier and take in the lay of the land and its strategic terrain.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉鄉試，學大進。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he passed the provincial examination, and his studies advanced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he passed the provincial examination, and his learning made great strides.

sentences.zh: 顧益好言兵，且善射。

translations.literal: Yet he increasingly loved to discourse on military affairs and was also skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He grew ever fonder of talking about warfare and was also an able archer.

sentences.zh: 登弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 12 (1499) he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 使治前威寧伯王越葬，還而朝議方急西北邊，守仁條八事上之。

translations.literal: He was sent to oversee the burial of the former Marquis of Weining, Wang Yue; on his return the court was urgently concerned about the northwest frontier, and Shouren submitted a memorial setting forth eight points.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to arrange the funeral of the late Marquis of Weining, Wang Yue; when he returned, court debate was focused on the northwest frontier, and Shouren memorialized eight proposals.

sentences.zh: 尋授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 決囚江北，引疾歸。

translations.literal: While hearing capital cases in northern Jiangsu he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After adjudicating capital cases in the Jianghuai north, he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 起補兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to fill a vacancy as principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 正德元年冬，劉瑾逮南京給事中御史戴銑等二十餘人。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhengde, Liu Jin arrested more than twenty Nanjing supervising secretaries and censors including Dai Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Zhengde 1 (1506), Liu Jin arrested more than twenty Nanjing supervising secretaries and censors, including Dai Xian.

sentences.zh: 守仁抗章救，瑾怒，廷杖四十，謫貴州龍場驛丞。

translations.literal: Shouren submitted a memorial in protest; Jin was enraged, had him beaten forty strokes at court, and banished him to be assistant magistrate at Longchang postal station in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren submitted a memorial in their defense; Jin was furious, had him beaten forty strokes in court, and banished him to assistant magistrate at Longchang Station in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 龍場萬山叢薄，苗、僚雜居。

translations.literal: Longchang lay amid thick mountain forests, with Miao and Lao peoples intermixed.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang was buried in dense mountain forest, with Miao and Lao peoples living intermingled.

sentences.zh: 守仁因俗化導，夷人喜，相率伐木為屋，以棲守仁。

translations.literal: Shouren guided them according to local custom; the tribesmen were pleased and together felled trees to build a house for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren civilized and instructed them according to local ways; the tribesmen were delighted and together cut timber to build a dwelling for him.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，量移廬陵知縣。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was transferred by degree to magistrate of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was put to death, Shouren was transferred to magistrate of Luling.

sentences.zh: 入覲，遷南京刑部主事，吏部尚書楊一清改之驗封。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court he was moved to principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing transferred him to the Seals and Credentials section.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself at court he was moved to principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; Minister Yang Yiqing reassigned him to the Seals and Credentials bureau.

sentences.zh: 屢遷考功郎中，擢南京太僕少卿，就遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, then appointed Junior Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud, and shortly afterward Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to director in the Bureau of Merit, was then made Junior Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud, and soon after Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王瓊素奇守仁才。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Qiong had long admired Shouren's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Qiong had long regarded Shouren's ability with wonder.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year (1516) he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 當是時，南中盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were springing up everywhere in the south.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were swarming across the southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 謝志山據橫水、左溪、桶岡，池仲容據浰頭，皆稱王 ，與大庾陳曰能、樂昌高快馬、郴州龔福全等攻剽府縣。

translations.literal: Xie Zhishan held Hengshui, Zuoxi, and Tonggang; Chi Zhongrong held Nantou; each styled himself king, and together with Chen Yueneng of Dayu, Gao Kuaima of Lechang, Gong Fuquan of Chenzhou, and others they raided prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhishan held Hengshui, Zuoxi, and Tonggang; Chi Zhongrong held Nantou; each called himself king, and with Chen Yueneng of Dayu, Gao Kuaima of Lechang, Gong Fuquan of Chenzhou, and others they plundered prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 而福建大帽山賊詹師富等又起。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the bandits of Damao Mountain in Fujian, Zhan Shifu and others, also rose.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the bandits of Damao Mountain in Fujian, led by Zhan Shifu, also rose up.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫文森托疾避去。

translations.literal: The previous grand coordinator Wen Sen pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The previous grand coordinator Wen Sen had pleaded illness and left the post.

sentences.zh: 志山合樂昌賊掠大庾，攻南康、贛州，贛縣主簿吳玭戰死。

translations.literal: Zhishan joined the Lechang bandits in plundering Dayu, attacked Nankang and Ganzhou, and the registrar of Ganzhen, Wu Yi, was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan allied with the Lechang bandits to raid Dayu and assault Nankang and Ganzhou; Wu Yi, registrar of Ganzhen, was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 守仁至，知左右多賊耳目，乃呼老黠隸詰之。

translations.literal: When Shouren arrived he knew that many around him were the bandits' eyes and ears, so he summoned an old crafty clerk and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren arrived he realized that many of those around him were the bandits' spies, and he summoned an old, shrewd clerk for questioning.

sentences.zh: 隸戰栗不敢隱，因貰其罪，令填賊，賊動靜無勿知。

translations.literal: The clerk trembled and dared not conceal anything; Shouren pardoned his crimes and ordered him to infiltrate the bandits, so that nothing of their movements escaped notice.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk trembled and dared conceal nothing; Shouren remitted his offenses and set him to infiltrate the bandits, so that their every move was known.

sentences.zh: 於是檄福建、廣東會兵，先討大帽山賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued orders for Fujian and Guangdong to assemble troops and first attacked the Damao Mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Fujian and Guangdong to muster troops and struck first at the Damao Mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，督副使楊璋等破賊長富村，逼之象湖山，指揮覃桓、縣丞紀鏞戰死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the vice commissioner Yang Zhang and others broke them at Changfu village and pressed them to Xianghu Mountain; the commander Tan Huan and the assistant magistrate Ji Yong were killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, under Vice Commissioner Yang Zhang and others, the bandits were broken at Changfu village and driven toward Xianghu Mountain; Commander Tan Huan and Assistant Magistrate Ji Yong fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 守仁親率銳卒屯上杭。

translations.literal: Shouren personally led elite troops and encamped at Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren personally led crack troops and encamped at Shanghang.

sentences.zh: 佯退師，出不意搗之，連破四十余寨，俘斬七千有奇，指揮王鎧等擒師富。

translations.literal: He feigned a withdrawal and struck unexpectedly, breaking more than forty stockades in succession, capturing and slaying more than seven thousand; the commander Wang Kai and others seized Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned a withdrawal and struck where they did not expect it, taking more than forty stockades in succession and capturing or killing more than seven thousand; Commander Wang Kai and others seized Shifu.

sentences.zh: 疏言權輕，無以令將士，請給旗牌，提督軍務，得便宜從事。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said his authority was too slight to command the officers and men, and asked for ceremonial banners and seals and overall supervision of military affairs with discretionary power.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said his authority was too light to command the troops and asked for banners of office, overall supervision of military affairs, and discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 尚書王瓊奏從其請。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Qiong memorialized that his request be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Qiong memorialized that his request be approved.

sentences.zh: 乃更兵制：二十五人為伍，伍有小甲；

translations.literal: He then reorganized the army: twenty-five men formed a squad, with a squad leader;
translations.idiomatic: He then reorganized the army: twenty-five men to a squad, each squad with a squad leader;

sentences.zh: 二伍為隊，隊有總甲；

translations.literal: two squads a platoon, with a platoon chief;
translations.idiomatic: two squads to a platoon, each platoon with a platoon chief;

sentences.zh: 四隊為哨，哨有長，協哨二佐之；

translations.literal: four platoons a sentry, with a sentry chief and two aides;
translations.idiomatic: four platoons to a sentry, each sentry with a chief and two assistants;

sentences.zh: 二哨為營，營有官，參謀二佐之；

translations.literal: two sentries a camp, with a camp officer and two staff aides;
translations.idiomatic: two sentries to a camp, each camp with an officer and two staff aides;

sentences.zh: 三營為陣，陣有偏將；

translations.literal: three camps a battle array, with a deputy commander;
translations.idiomatic: three camps to a battle array, each array with a deputy commander;

sentences.zh: 二陣為軍，軍有副將。

translations.literal: two arrays an army, with a vice general.
translations.idiomatic: two arrays to an army, each army with a vice general.

sentences.zh: 皆臨事委，不命於朝；

translations.literal: All were appointed on campaign and received no orders from court;
translations.idiomatic: All were appointed on the spot for the campaign and took no orders from the capital;

sentences.zh: 副將以下，得遞相罰治。

translations.literal: below the vice general, each rank could successively punish those beneath.
translations.idiomatic: and below the vice general each rank could discipline the ranks beneath it in turn.

sentences.zh: 其年七月進兵大庾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he advanced into Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the seventh month, he marched into Dayu.

sentences.zh: 志山乘間急攻南安，知府季斅擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhishan seized the interval to press urgently against Nan'an; the prefect Ji Que defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishan seized an opening to press hard on Nan'an; Prefect Ji Que defeated him.

sentences.zh: 副使楊璋等亦生縶曰能以歸。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Yang Zhang and others also captured Chen Yueneng alive and brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Yang Zhang and others also took Chen Yueneng alive and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 遂議討橫水、左溪。

translations.literal: They thereupon planned an expedition against Hengshui and Zuoxi.
translations.idiomatic: They then planned a campaign against Hengshui and Zuoxi.

sentences.zh: 十月，都指揮許清、贛州知府邢珣、寧都知縣王天與各一軍會橫水，斅及守備郟文、汀州知府唐淳、縣丞舒富各一軍會左溪，吉安知府伍文定、程鄉知縣張戩遏其奔軼。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the regional commander Xu Qing, the prefect of Ganzhou Xing Qi, and the magistrate of Ningdu Wang Tianyu each led an army to Hengshui; Ji Que and the garrison commander Zou Wen, the prefect of Tingzhou Tang Chun, and the assistant magistrate Shu Fu each led an army to Zuoxi; the prefect of Ji'an Wu Wendading and the magistrate of Chengxiang Zhang Xian blocked their escape.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Regional Commander Xu Qing, Ganzhou Prefect Xing Qi, and Ningdu Magistrate Wang Tianyu each led a force to Hengshui; Ji Que, Garrison Commander Zou Wen, Tingzhou Prefect Tang Chun, and Assistant Magistrate Shu Fu each led a force to Zuoxi; Ji'an Prefect Wu Wendading and Chengxiang Magistrate Zhang Xian cut off their escape.

sentences.zh: 守仁自駐南康 ，去橫水三十里，先遣四百人伏賊巢左右，進軍逼之。

translations.literal: Shouren himself stayed at Nankang thirty li from Hengshui, first sent four hundred men to ambush both sides of the bandit nest, and advanced to press them.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren himself held Nankang, thirty li from Hengshui, first sent four hundred men to lie in ambush on either side of the bandit lair, then advanced to press them.

sentences.zh: 賊方迎戰，兩山舉幟。

translations.literal: The bandits were just meeting the attack when banners were raised on both hills.
translations.idiomatic: As the bandits came out to fight, banners rose on both hills.

sentences.zh: 賊大驚，謂官軍已盡犁其巢，遂潰。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly alarmed, thinking the government army had already uprooted their nest entirely, and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were terrified, believing the government troops had already overrun their lair, and broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 乘勝克橫水，志山及其黨蕭貴模等皆走桶岡。

translations.literal: Pressing the advantage they took Hengshui; Zhishan and his follower Xiao Guimo and others all fled to Tonggang.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory they took Hengshui; Zhishan and his followers Xiao Guimo and the rest all fled to Tonggang.

sentences.zh: 左溪亦破。

translations.literal: Zuoxi was also broken.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoxi fell as well.

sentences.zh: 守仁以桶岡險固，移營近地，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Shouren held that Tonggang was steep and solid; he moved his camp nearer and admonished them on fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren judged Tonggang steep and strong, moved his camp closer, and admonished the bandits on the consequences of fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 賊首藍廷鳳等方震恐，見使至大喜，期仲冬朔降，而珣、文定已冒雨奪險入。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftains Lan Tingfeng and others were just terrified; when the envoy arrived they were greatly pleased and set the first day of the eleventh month for surrender, but Xing and Wendading had already seized the perilous passes in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leaders Lan Tingfeng and the rest were already shaken with fear; when the envoy came they were overjoyed and set the first day of the eleventh month to surrender, but Xing and Wendading had already forced the passes in the rain.

sentences.zh: 賊阻水陣，珣直前搏戰，文定與戩自右出，賊倉卒敗走，遇淳兵又敗。

translations.literal: The bandits arrayed across the water; Xing charged forward to grapple; Wendading and Zhang came out on the right; the bandits were defeated in haste and, meeting Tang Chun's force, were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits formed a line across the water; Xing charged straight in to grapple; Wendading and Zhang came out on the right; the bandits broke in confusion, and meeting Tang Chun's troops were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 諸軍破桶岡，志山、貴模、廷鳳面縛降。

translations.literal: The various armies broke Tonggang; Zhishan, Guimo, and Tingfeng came forward bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The combined forces broke Tonggang; Zhishan, Guimo, and Tingfeng came forward with bound hands to surrender.

sentences.zh: 凡破巢八十有四，俘斬六千有奇。

translations.literal: In all they destroyed eighty-four nests and captured and killed more than six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In all they destroyed eighty-four lairs and captured or killed more than six thousand.

sentences.zh: 時湖廣巡撫秦金亦破福全。

translations.literal: At that time the Huguang grand coordinator Qin Jin had also broken Fuquan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Huguang Grand Coordinator Qin Jin had also defeated Fuquan.

sentences.zh: 其黨千人突至，諸將擒斬之。

translations.literal: A thousand of his followers made a sudden raid; the generals captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand of his followers made a sudden thrust; the generals captured and killed them.

sentences.zh: 乃設崇義縣於橫水，控諸瑤。

translations.literal: They then established Chongyi County at Hengshui to control the various Yao.
translations.idiomatic: They then established Chongyi County at Hengshui to keep the Yao peoples in check.

sentences.zh: 還至贛州，議討浰頭賊。

translations.literal: Returning to Ganzhou they planned to attack the Nantou bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Ganzhou they planned an expedition against the Nantou bandits.

sentences.zh: 初，守仁之平師富也，龍川賊盧珂、鄭志高、陳英咸請降。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouren had pacified Shifu, the Longchuan bandits Lu Ke, Zheng Zhigao, and Chen Ying had all asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shouren had pacified Shifu, the Longchuan bandits Lu Ke, Zheng Zhigao, and Chen Ying had all offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 及征橫水，浰頭賊將黃金巢亦以五百人降 ，獨仲容未下。

translations.literal: When he campaigned against Hengshui, the Nantou bandit general Huang Jinchao also surrendered with five hundred men, but Zhongrong alone had not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Hengshui, the Nantou bandit commander Huang Jinchao also surrendered with five hundred men, but Zhongrong alone had not submitted.

sentences.zh: 橫水破，仲容始遣弟仲安來歸，而嚴為戰守備。

translations.literal: After Hengshui fell, Zhongrong at last sent his younger brother Zhong'an to submit, yet he strictly prepared for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Hengshui fell, Zhongrong at last sent his younger brother Zhong'an to submit, yet he kept his defenses tight for war.

sentences.zh: 詭言：「珂、志高，仇也，將襲我，故為備。」

translations.literal: He falsely said: "Ke and Zhigao are my enemies and will attack me, so I make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed: "Ke and Zhigao are my enemies and mean to strike me, so I must prepare.

sentences.zh: 守仁佯杖系珂等，而陰使珂弟集兵待，遂下令散兵。

translations.literal: Shouren feigned beating and imprisoning Ke and the others, but secretly had Ke's younger brother gather troops and wait; he then ordered the armies dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren pretended to beat and bind Ke and the others, but secretly had Ke's younger brother muster troops in readiness, then ordered the army disbanded.

sentences.zh: 歲首大張燈樂，仲容信且疑。

translations.literal: At New Year he set out lanterns and music on a grand scale; Zhongrong believed yet doubted.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year he staged lanterns and music on a grand scale; Zhongrong half believed and half doubted.

sentences.zh: 守仁賜以節物，誘入謝。

translations.literal: Shouren bestowed ceremonial gifts and lured him to come in to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren gave him festival gifts and lured him in to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 仲容率九十三人營教場，而自以數人入謁。

translations.literal: Zhongrong led ninety-three men to camp at the drill ground while he himself entered with only a few men to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong led ninety-three men to encamp on the drill ground while he himself came in with only a few men to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 守仁呵之曰：「若皆吾民，屯於外，疑我乎？」

translations.literal: Shouren rebuked him: "If you are all my people, why do you camp outside—do you doubt me?
translations.idiomatic: Shouren rebuked him: "If you are all my people, why camp outside—do you doubt me?

sentences.zh: 悉引入祥符宮，厚飲食之。

translations.literal: He had them all brought into Xiangfu Palace and generously feasted them.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all brought into Xiangfu Palace and gave them a lavish feast.

sentences.zh: 賊大喜過望，益自安。

translations.literal: The bandits were delighted beyond expectation and grew more at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were delighted beyond all expectation and grew still more at ease.

sentences.zh: 守仁留仲容觀燈樂。

translations.literal: Shouren detained Zhongrong to watch the lanterns and music.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren kept Zhongrong to watch the lanterns and music.

sentences.zh: 正月三日大享，伏甲士於門，諸賊入，以次悉擒戮之。

translations.literal: On the third day of the first month he held a grand feast; armed men lay hidden at the gate; the bandits entered and were seized and executed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the first month he held a great feast; armed men lay hidden at the gate; as the bandits entered they were seized and killed one after another.

sentences.zh: 自將抵賊巢，連破上、中、下三浰，斬馘二千有奇。

translations.literal: He himself led troops against the bandit nest, breaking in succession the upper, middle, and lower Nantou, and cutting heads and ears numbering more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led troops against the bandit lair, taking in succession the upper, middle, and lower Nantou, and killing more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 余賊奔九連山。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled to Jiulian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bandits fled to Jiulian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 山橫亙數百里，陡絕不可攻。

translations.literal: The mountain stretched several hundred li, precipitous and impossible to assault.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain ran several hundred li, sheer and impossible to assault.

sentences.zh: 乃簡壯士七百人衣賊衣，奔崖下，賊招之上。

translations.literal: He then selected seven hundred stalwart men dressed in bandit garb to rush down the cliff; the bandits called them up.
translations.idiomatic: He then picked seven hundred stalwart men, dressed them in bandit clothing, and sent them racing down the cliff; the bandits beckoned them up.

sentences.zh: 官軍進攻，內外合擊，擒斬無遺。

translations.literal: The government troops attacked from without while those within struck together; none were left to capture or kill.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops attacked from without while those within struck together; not one was left alive.

sentences.zh: 乃於下浰立和平縣，置戍而歸。

translations.literal: He then established Heping County at lower Nantou, posted garrison troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then established Heping County at lower Nantou, posted a garrison, and returned.

sentences.zh: 自是境內大定。

translations.literal: From then on the whole region was greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the whole region was at peace.

sentences.zh: 初，朝議賊勢強，發廣東、湖廣兵合剿。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had judged the bandits' power strong and ordered troops from Guangdong and Huguang to join in extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had judged the bandits too strong and ordered troops from Guangdong and Huguang to join in a combined suppression.

sentences.zh: 守仁上疏止之，不及。

translations.literal: Shouren memorialized to stop this, but it did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren memorialized to halt this, but too late.

sentences.zh: 桶岡既滅，湖廣兵始至。

translations.literal: After Tonggang was destroyed, the Huguang troops only then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After Tonggang had been destroyed, the Huguang troops only then arrived.

sentences.zh: 及平浰頭 ，廣東尚未承檄。

translations.literal: When Nantou was pacified, Guangdong had still not received the dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Nantou was pacified, Guangdong had still not received the order.

sentences.zh: 守仁所將皆文吏及偏裨小校，平數十年巨寇，遠近驚為神。

translations.literal: The troops Shouren led were all civil officials and junior officers; he pacified bandits of decades' standing, and near and far they marveled at him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: The men Shouren led were all civil officials and junior officers, yet he pacified bandits that had plagued the region for decades, and people near and far hailed him as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，予世襲錦衣衛百戶，再進副千戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted a hereditary hundred-household post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and later advanced to deputy thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted a hereditary hundred-household post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and later advanced to deputy thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，命勘福建叛軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was ordered to investigate the Fujian rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was ordered to investigate the Fujian rebels.

sentences.zh: 行至豐城而寧王宸濠反，知縣顧佖以告。

translations.literal: When he reached Fengcheng the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled; the magistrate Gu Yi reported it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Fengcheng he learned that the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, had rebelled; Magistrate Gu Yi brought him the news.

sentences.zh: 守仁急趨吉安，與伍文定征調兵食，治器械舟楫 ，傳檄暴宸濠罪，俾守令各率吏士勤王。

translations.literal: Shouren hurried to Ji'an, and with Wu Wendading mobilized troops and provisions, prepared weapons and boats, issued proclamations exposing Chen Hao's crimes, and ordered prefects and magistrates each to lead clerks and soldiers to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren hurried to Ji'an, and with Wu Wendading raised troops and supplies, prepared arms and boats, issued proclamations exposing Chen Hao's crimes, and ordered every prefect and magistrate to lead clerks and soldiers to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 都御史王懋中，編修鄒守益，副使羅循、羅欽德，郎中曾直，御史張鰲山、周魯，評事羅僑，同知郭祥鵬，進士郭持平，降謫驛丞王思、李中，咸赴守仁軍。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Maozhong, Hanlin compiler Zou Shouyi, vice commissioners Luo Xun and Luo Qinde, director Zeng Zhi, censors Zhang Aoshan and Zhou Lu, judicial reviewer Luo Qiao, subprefect Guo Xiangpeng, jinshi Guo Chiping, and the demoted postal assistant magistrates Wang Si and Li Zhong all came to Shouren's army.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Maozhong, Hanlin compiler Zou Shouyi, Vice Commissioners Luo Xun and Luo Qinde, Director Zeng Zhi, Censors Zhang Aoshan and Zhou Lu, Judicial Reviewer Luo Qiao, Subprefect Guo Xiangpeng, Jinshi Guo Chiping, and the demoted postal assistant magistrates Wang Si and Li Zhong all joined Shouren's army.

sentences.zh: 御史謝源、伍希儒自廣東還，守仁留之紀功。

translations.literal: The censors Xie Yuan and Wu Xiru, returning from Guangdong, were retained by Shouren to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xie Yuan and Wu Xiru, returning from Guangdong, Shouren kept to record achievements.

sentences.zh: 因集眾議曰：「賊若出長江順流東下，則南都不可保。

translations.literal: He then assembled the host for counsel and said: "If the rebels sail down the Yangzi with the current toward the east, the southern capital cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered his officers and said: "If the rebels sail down the Yangzi with the current toward the east, the southern capital cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 吾欲以計撓之，少遲旬日無患矣。」

translations.literal: I wish to use stratagem to thwart them; if we delay them a little more than ten days there will be no worry.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to thwart them by stratagem; if we delay them a fortnight or so, we need not worry.

sentences.zh: 乃多遣間諜，檄府縣言：「都督許泰、郤永將邊兵，都督劉暉、桂勇將京兵，各四萬，水陸併進。

translations.literal: He then sent out many spies and issued orders to prefectures and counties saying: "Regional commanders Xu Tai and Xi Yong will lead frontier troops, regional commanders Liu Hui and Gui Yong will lead capital troops, forty thousand each, advancing together by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent out many spies and issued orders to prefectures and counties saying: "Regional Commanders Xu Tai and Xi Yong will lead frontier troops, Regional Commanders Liu Hui and Gui Yong will lead capital troops, forty thousand each, advancing together by land and water.

sentences.zh: 南贛王守仁、湖廣秦金、兩廣楊旦各率所部合十六萬，直搗南昌，所至有司缺供者，以軍法論。」

translations.literal: Wang Shouren of southern Jiangxi, Qin Jin of Huguang, and Yang Dan of the two Guang each leading their forces, totaling one hundred sixty thousand, will strike straight at Nanchang; wherever officials fail in supplies, military law will apply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren of southern Jiangxi, Qin Jin of Huguang, and Yang Dan of the two Guang, each leading his forces for a combined total of one hundred sixty thousand, will strike straight at Nanchang; wherever officials fail in supplies, military law will apply.

sentences.zh: 又為蠟書遺偽相李士實、劉養正，敘其歸國之誠，令從臾早發兵東下，而縱諜泄之。

translations.literal: He also wrote a wax-sealed letter to the false chancellors Li Shishi and Liu Yangzheng, stating their sincerity in returning to the realm and urging them to hasten the army eastward, then deliberately let spies leak it.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a wax-sealed letter to the rebel chancellors Li Shishi and Liu Yangzheng, professing their loyalty to the realm and urging them to hurry the army eastward, then deliberately let spies leak it.

sentences.zh: 宸濠果疑。

translations.literal: Chen Hao indeed grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao did grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 與士實、養正謀，則皆勸之疾趨南京即大位，宸濠益大疑。

translations.literal: When he consulted with Shishi and Yangzheng, they all urged him to hurry to Nanjing and take the throne; Chen Hao grew still more suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When he consulted Shishi and Yangzheng, they all urged him to hurry to Nanjing and seize the throne; Chen Hao grew still more suspicious.

sentences.zh: 十余日詗知中外兵不至，乃悟守仁紿之。

translations.literal: After more than ten days of inquiry he learned that troops from within and without had not arrived, and then realized Shouren had deceived him.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of inquiry he learned that no troops from within or without were coming, and then realized Shouren had deceived him.

sentences.zh: 七月壬辰朔，留宜春王拱嵒居守，而劫其眾六萬人，襲下九江、南康，出大江，薄安慶。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, ren-chen, he left the Prince of Yichun, Gong Yan, to hold the city, seized his host of sixty thousand, stormed Jiujiang and Nankang, entered the great river, and pressed upon Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month he left the Prince of Yichun, Gong Yan, to hold the city, seized his host of sixty thousand, stormed Jiujiang and Nankang, entered the great river, and pressed upon Anqing.

sentences.zh: 守仁聞南昌兵少則大喜，趨樟樹鎮。

translations.literal: When Shouren heard that Nanchang had few troops he was greatly pleased and hurried to Zhangshu town.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren heard that Nanchang was lightly garrisoned he was greatly pleased and hurried to Zhangshu.

sentences.zh: 知府臨江戴德孺、袁州徐璉、贛州邢珣，都指揮余恩，通判瑞州胡堯元、童琦、撫州鄒琥、安吉談儲，推官王、徐文英，知縣新淦李美、泰和李楫、萬安王冕、寧都王天與，各以兵來會，合八萬人，號三十萬。

translations.literal: The prefect of Linjiang Dai Deru, of Yuanzhou Xu Lian, of Ganzhou Xing Qi, regional commander Yu En, subprefects of Ruizhou Hu Yaoyuan and Tong Qi, of Fuzhou Zou Hu, of Anji Tan Chu, judicial reviewers Wang and Xu Wenyin, magistrates of Xingan Li Mei, of Taihe Li Ji, of Wan'an Wang Mian, and of Ningdu Wang Tianyu each came with troops to join; together they numbered eighty thousand and proclaimed three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Dai Deru of Linjiang, Xu Lian of Yuanzhou, Xing Qi of Ganzhou, Regional Commander Yu En, Subprefects Hu Yaoyuan and Tong Qi of Ruizhou, Zou Hu of Fuzhou, Tan Chu of Anji, Judicial Reviewers Wang and Xu Wenyin, and Magistrates Li Mei of Xingan, Li Ji of Taihe, Wang Mian of Wan'an, and Wang Tianyu of Ningdu each came with troops; together they numbered eighty thousand and proclaimed three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 或請救安慶，守仁曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Some urged rescuing Anqing; Shouren said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged rescuing Anqing; Shouren said: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 今九江、南康已為賊守，我越南昌與相持江上，二郡兵絕我後，是腹背受敵也。

translations.literal: Now Jiujiang and Nankang are already held by the rebels; if we cross south of Nanchang and face them on the river, the troops of the two prefectures will cut off our rear—this is to be attacked front and back.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang and Nankang are already in rebel hands; if we cross south of Nanchang and face them on the river, the troops of those two prefectures will cut off our rear—we would be caught between two fires.

sentences.zh: 不如直搗南昌。

translations.literal: Better to strike straight at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike straight at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 賊精銳悉出，守備虛。

translations.literal: The rebels' elite troops have all gone out; the garrison is empty.
translations.idiomatic: Their crack troops have all marched out; the garrison is empty.

sentences.zh: 我軍新集氣銳，攻必破。

translations.literal: Our army is newly gathered and keen in spirit; if we attack we are sure to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Our army is freshly gathered and full of fight; attack and we are sure to take it.

sentences.zh: 賊聞南昌破，必解圍自救。

translations.literal: When the rebels hear Nanchang has fallen they are sure to lift the siege to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels hear Nanchang has fallen they are sure to lift the siege and hurry back.

sentences.zh: 逆擊之湖中，蔑不勝矣。」

translations.literal: If we meet them in the lake and strike, there is none we cannot overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Meet them on the lake and strike, and we cannot fail to win.

sentences.zh: 眾曰「善」。

translations.literal: The host said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 己酉次豐城，以文定為前鋒，選遣奉新知縣劉守緒襲其伏兵。

translations.literal: On ji-you he halted at Fengcheng, made Wendading vanguard, and selected and sent the magistrate of Fengxin, Liu Shouxu, to strike their ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-you he halted at Fengcheng, made Wendading vanguard, and sent Fengxin Magistrate Liu Shouxu to strike their ambush troops.

sentences.zh: 庚戌夜半，文定兵抵廣潤門，守兵駭散。

translations.literal: At midnight on geng-xu Wendading's troops reached the Guangrun Gate; the garrison troops fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on geng-xu Wendading's troops reached the Guangrun Gate; the garrison broke and fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 辛亥黎明，諸軍梯糹亙登，縛拱嵒等，宮人多焚死。

translations.literal: At dawn on xin-hai the various armies climbed scaling ladders; they bound Gong Yan and others; many palace women were burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on xin-hai the various armies climbed scaling ladders, bound Gong Yan and the rest, and many palace women perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 軍士頗殺掠，守仁戮犯令者十餘人，宥脅從，安士民，慰諭宗室，人心乃悅。

translations.literal: The soldiers engaged in considerable killing and plunder; Shouren executed more than ten who violated orders, pardoned those coerced to follow, reassured scholars and commoners, and comforted the imperial clan; hearts were then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers killed and plundered freely; Shouren executed more than ten who violated orders, pardoned those who had been coerced, reassured scholars and commoners, and comforted the imperial clan, and the people were won over.

sentences.zh: 居二日，遣文定、珣、璉、德孺各將精兵分道進，而使堯元等設伏。

translations.literal: After two days he sent Wendading, Xing, Lian, and Deru each leading elite troops by separate routes, while Yaoyuan and others set ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he sent Wendading, Xing, Lian, and Deru each leading crack troops by separate routes, while Yaoyuan and others lay in ambush.

sentences.zh: 宸濠果自安慶還兵。

translations.literal: Chen Hao indeed returned his troops from Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao did return his troops from Anqing.

sentences.zh: 乙卯遇於黃家渡。

translations.literal: On yi-mao they met at Huangjia Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-mao they met at Huangjia Ford.

sentences.zh: 文定當其前鋒，賊趨利。

translations.literal: Wendading met their vanguard; the rebels rushed for advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Wendading met their vanguard; the rebels rushed to seize the advantage.

sentences.zh: 珣繞出賊背貫其中，文定、恩乘之 ，璉、德孺張兩翼分賊勢，堯元等伏發，賊大潰，退保八字腦。

translations.literal: Xing circled behind the rebels and pierced their center; Wendading and En pressed the advantage; Lian and Deru spread both wings to divide the rebel force; Yaoyuan and others sprang the ambush; the rebels fled in great disorder and retreated to hold Bazinao.
translations.idiomatic: Xing swung around behind the rebels and drove through their center; Wendading and En pressed the attack; Lian and Deru spread both wings to split the rebel force; Yaoyuan and others sprang the ambush; the rebels broke and fled, falling back to hold Bazinao.

sentences.zh: 宸濠懼，盡發南康、九江兵。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was afraid and sent out all the troops of Nankang and Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao was afraid and threw out every soldier from Nankang and Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 守仁遣知府撫州陳槐、饒州林城取九江，建昌曾璵、廣信周朝佐取南康。

translations.literal: Shouren sent the prefect of Fuzhou Chen Huai and of Raozhou Lin Cheng to take Jiujiang, and Zeng Yu of Jianchang and Zhou Chaozuo of Guangxin to take Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren sent Fuzhou Prefect Chen Huai and Raozhou Prefect Lin Cheng to take Jiujiang, and Zeng Yu of Jianchang and Zhou Chaozuo of Guangxin to take Nankang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰復戰，官軍卻，守仁斬先卻者。

translations.literal: On bing-chen they fought again; the government army fell back; Shouren executed those who retreated first.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-chen they fought again; the government troops fell back; Shouren executed those who retreated first.

sentences.zh: 諸軍殊死戰，賊復大敗。

translations.literal: The various armies fought to the death; the rebels were again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The various armies fought to the death; the rebels were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 退保樵舍，聯舟為方陣，盡出金寶犒士。

translations.literal: They retreated to hold Qiaoshe, linked boats into a square formation, and poured out all gold and treasure to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They fell back to Qiaoshe, lashed their boats into a square formation, and poured out all their gold and treasure to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 明日，宸濠方晨朝其群臣，官軍奄至。

translations.literal: The next day Chen Hao was just holding morning court with his ministers when the government army arrived suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chen Hao was just holding morning court with his ministers when the government army fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 以小舟載薪，乘風縱火，焚其副舟，妃婁氏以下皆投水死。

translations.literal: With small boats loaded with kindling they rode the wind to set fires, burning the secondary boats; the consort Lou and those below all threw themselves into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Small boats loaded with kindling rode the wind to set fires and burn the secondary boats; Consort Lou and those below all threw themselves into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 宸濠舟膠淺，倉卒易舟遁，王冕所部兵追執之。

translations.literal: Chen Hao's boat ran aground in shallow water; in haste he changed boats to flee; the troops under Wang Mian pursued and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao's boat ran aground in the shallows; in haste he changed boats to flee; Wang Mian's troops pursued and seized him.

sentences.zh: 士實、養正及降賊按察使楊璋等皆就擒。

translations.literal: Shishi, Yangzheng, and the surrendered rebel surveillance commissioner Yang Zhang and others were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi, Yangzheng, and the surrendered rebel Surveillance Commissioner Yang Zhang and others were all taken.

sentences.zh: 南康、九江亦下。

translations.literal: Nankang and Jiujiang also fell.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang and Jiujiang fell as well.

sentences.zh: 凡三十五日而賊平。

translations.literal: In all, within thirty-five days the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty-five days the rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 京師聞變，諸大臣震懼。

translations.literal: When the capital heard of the uprising, the various ministers were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital heard of the uprising, the ministers were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 王瓊大言曰：「王伯安居南昌上游，必擒賊。」

translations.literal: Wang Qiong spoke loudly: "Wang Bo'an holds the upper reaches of Nanchang; he is sure to capture the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong declared loudly: "Wang Bo'an holds the upper Yangzi above Nanchang; he is sure to capture the rebels.

sentences.zh: 至是，果奏捷。

translations.literal: By then, victory was indeed reported.
translations.idiomatic: And by then victory was indeed reported.

sentences.zh: 帝時已親征，自稱「威武大將軍」，率京邊驍卒數萬南下。

translations.literal: The emperor had already gone on campaign in person, styling himself "Grand General of Martial Prestige," and led tens of thousands of crack troops from the capital and frontier southward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already gone on campaign in person, styling himself Grand General of Martial Prestige, and led tens of thousands of crack troops from the capital and frontier southward.

sentences.zh: 命安邊伯許泰為副將軍，偕提督軍務太監張忠、平賊將軍左都督劉暉將京軍數千，溯江而上 ，抵南昌。

translations.literal: He appointed the Earl Who Pacifies the Frontier, Xu Tai, vice general, who together with the eunuch Zhang Zhong, supervisor of military affairs, and the Pacification General, Left Regional Commander Liu Hui, led several thousand capital troops up the river and reached Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the Earl Who Pacifies the Frontier, Xu Tai, vice general; together with the eunuch Zhang Zhong, supervisor of military affairs, and the Pacification General, Left Regional Commander Liu Hui, they led several thousand capital troops up the river to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖幸故與宸濠通，守仁初上宸濠反書，因言：「覬覦者非特一寧王，請黜奸諛以回天下豪傑心。」

translations.literal: The various favored minions had long been in communication with Chen Hao; when Shouren first memorialized on Chen Hao's rebellion he also said: "Those who covet the throne are not only the Prince of Ning; I beg that sycophants and flatterers be dismissed to win back the hearts of heroes throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites had long been in league with Chen Hao; when Shouren first reported the rebellion he also wrote: "Those who covet the throne are not only the Prince of Ning; dismiss the sycophants and flatterers to win back the hearts of heroes throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖幸皆恨。

translations.literal: The various favored minions all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: The favorites all hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 宸濠既平，則相與媢功。

translations.literal: Once Chen Hao was pacified, they joined together to claim the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Hao was defeated, they joined together to claim the credit.

sentences.zh: 且懼守仁見天子發其罪，競為蜚語，謂守仁先與通謀，慮事不成，乃起兵。

translations.literal: Moreover they feared that if Shouren saw the Son of Heaven he would expose their crimes; they competed in spreading slander, saying Shouren had first conspired with Chen Hao and, fearing the affair would fail, then raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: They also feared that if Shouren saw the emperor he would expose their crimes; they spread slander far and wide, saying Shouren had first conspired with Chen Hao and, fearing failure, then raised troops.

sentences.zh: 又欲令縱宸濠湖中，待帝自擒。

translations.literal: They also wished to have Chen Hao released on the lake so the emperor could capture him himself.
translations.idiomatic: They also wanted Chen Hao released on the lake so the emperor could capture him himself.

sentences.zh: 守仁乘忠、泰未至，先俘宸濠，發南昌。

translations.literal: Before Zhong and Tai arrived, Shouren first captured Chen Hao and set out from Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhong and Tai arrived, Shouren captured Chen Hao first and set out from Nanchang with him.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰以威武大將軍檄邀之廣信。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai, by order of the Grand General of Martial Prestige, invited him to Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai, by order of the Grand General of Martial Prestige, summoned him to Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 守仁不與，間道趨玉山，上書請獻俘，止帝南征。

translations.literal: Shouren did not go; by a side road he hurried to Yushan and memorialized asking to present the captive and halt the emperor's southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren refused; by a side road he hurried to Yushan and memorialized asking to present the captive and halt the emperor's southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 至錢唐遇太監張永。

translations.literal: When he reached Qiantang he met the eunuch Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiantang he met the eunuch Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 永提督贊畫機密軍務，在忠、泰輩上，而故與楊一清善，除劉瑾，天下稱之。

translations.literal: Yong supervised planning of secret military affairs and stood above Zhong, Tai, and their sort; he was also old friends with Yang Yiqing and had helped remove Liu Jin, for which the realm praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong supervised secret military planning and outranked Zhong, Tai, and their sort; he was also old friends with Yang Yiqing and had helped remove Liu Jin, for which the realm praised him.

sentences.zh: 守仁夜見永，頌其賢，因極言江西困敝，不堪六師擾。

translations.literal: Shouren visited Yong by night, praised his worth, and spoke at length of how exhausted Jiangxi was and could not bear the disturbance of the six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren visited Yong by night, praised his worth, and spoke at length of how exhausted Jiangxi was and could not bear the disturbance of the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 永深然之，曰：「永此來，為調護聖躬，非邀功也。

translations.literal: Yong deeply agreed and said: "I have come to safeguard the sacred person, not to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yong deeply agreed and said: "I have come to safeguard the emperor's person, not to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 公大勛，永知之，但事不可直情耳。」

translations.literal: Your great merit Yong knows, but the affair cannot follow straightforward feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Your great merit I know well, but the affair cannot follow straightforward feeling.

sentences.zh: 守仁乃以宸濠付永，而身至京口，欲朝行在。

translations.literal: Shouren then handed Chen Hao over to Yong and himself went to Jingkou, wishing to attend court at the imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren then handed Chen Hao over to Yong and himself went to Jingkou, wishing to attend the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 聞巡撫江西命，乃還南昌。

translations.literal: On hearing he was appointed grand coordinator of Jiangxi, he returned to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing he had been appointed grand coordinator of Jiangxi, he returned to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰已先至，恨失宸濠。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai had already arrived first and resented having lost Chen Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai had already arrived and resented having lost Chen Hao.

sentences.zh: 故縱京軍犯守仁，或呼名嫚罵。

translations.literal: They therefore let the capital troops harass Shouren, some calling his name and reviling him.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore let the capital troops harass Shouren, some calling his name and reviling him.

sentences.zh: 守仁不為動，撫之愈厚。

translations.literal: Shouren was unmoved and treated them all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was unmoved and treated them all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 病予藥，死予棺，遭喪於道，必停車慰問良久始去。

translations.literal: If they were ill he gave medicine; if they died he gave coffins; if they met with mourning on the road he always halted his carriage to console them at length before departing.
translations.idiomatic: If they fell ill he gave them medicine; if they died he gave them coffins; if they met with mourning on the road he always halted his carriage to console them at length before moving on.

sentences.zh: 京軍謂「王都堂愛我」，無復犯者。

translations.literal: The capital troops said, "Commissioner Wang loves us," and none again offended.
translations.idiomatic: The capital troops said, "Commissioner Wang cares for us," and none offended him again.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰言：「寧府富厚甲天下，今所蓄安在？」

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai said: "The Ning princely establishment's wealth topped the realm; where is what was stored now?
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai said: "The Prince of Ning's wealth topped the realm; where is what he stored now?

sentences.zh: 守仁曰：「宸濠異時盡以輸京師要人，約內應，籍可按也。」

translations.literal: Shouren said: "Chen Hao long ago gave it all to powerful men in the capital, arranging for inside response; the registers can be checked."
translations.idiomatic: Shouren said: "Chen Hao long ago gave it all to powerful men in the capital, arranging for inside collusion; the registers can be checked."

sentences.zh: 忠、泰故嘗納宸濠賄者，氣懾不敢復言。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai had formerly accepted bribes from Chen Hao; their spirits were cowed and they dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai had themselves accepted bribes from Chen Hao; cowed, they dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 已，輕守仁文士，強之射。

translations.literal: Later, despising Shouren as a literary man, they forced him to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Later, despising Shouren as a mere scholar, they forced him to shoot.

sentences.zh: 徐起，三發三中。

translations.literal: He rose slowly, and with three shots hit the target three times.
translations.idiomatic: He rose slowly and with three shots hit the target three times.

sentences.zh: 京軍皆歡呼，忠、泰益沮。

translations.literal: The capital troops all cheered; Zhong and Tai grew still more dejected.
translations.idiomatic: The capital troops all cheered; Zhong and Tai grew still more dejected.

sentences.zh: 會冬至，守仁命居民巷祭，已，上冢哭。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice Shouren ordered the residents to perform lane sacrifices; afterward he went up to the tombs and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice Shouren ordered the residents to perform lane sacrifices; afterward he went to the tombs and wept.

sentences.zh: 時新喪亂，悲號震野。

translations.literal: The realm had just suffered rebellion and mourning; cries of grief shook the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The land had just been torn by rebellion and mourning; cries of grief shook the open country.

sentences.zh: 京軍離家久，聞之無不泣下思歸者。

translations.literal: The capital troops had been long from home; hearing this, none failed to weep and long to return.
translations.idiomatic: The capital troops had been long from home; hearing this, every one of them wept and longed to return.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰不得已班師。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai had no choice but to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai had no choice but to withdraw the army.

sentences.zh: 比見帝，與紀功給事中祝續、御史章綸讒毀百端，獨永時時左右之。

translations.literal: When they saw the emperor, together with the merit-recording supervising secretary Zhu Xu and censor Zhang Lun they slandered him in every way; only Yong from time to time supported him.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw the emperor, together with Merit-Recording Supervising Secretary Zhu Xu and Censor Zhang Lun they slandered him in every way; only Yong from time to time spoke in his favor.

sentences.zh: 忠揚言帝前曰：「守仁必反，試召之，必不至。」

translations.literal: Zhong declared before the emperor: "Shouren is sure to rebel; try summoning him—he is sure not to come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong declared before the emperor: "Shouren is sure to rebel; try summoning him—he will not come.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰屢矯旨召守仁。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai repeatedly forged orders summoning Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai repeatedly forged orders summoning Shouren.

sentences.zh: 守仁得永密信，不赴。

translations.literal: Shouren received Yong's secret letter and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren received Yong's secret letter and did not go.

sentences.zh: 及是知出帝意，立馳至。

translations.literal: When he learned this came from the emperor's intent he immediately galloped to attend.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned this came from the emperor himself he galloped to attend at once.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰計沮，不令見帝。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai's plot was thwarted; they did not let him see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai's plot was thwarted; they would not let him see the emperor.

sentences.zh: 守仁乃入九華山，日晏坐僧寺。

translations.literal: Shouren then entered Jiuhua Mountain and at day's end sat in a monk's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren then withdrew to Jiuhua Mountain and at day's end sat in a monk's temple.

sentences.zh: 帝覘知之，曰：「王守仁學道人，聞召即至，何謂反？」

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and said: "Wang Shouren is a man who studies the Way; hearing a summons he comes at once—how can he be called a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and said: "Wang Shouren is a man who studies the Way; hearing a summons he comes at once—how can he be called a rebel?

sentences.zh: 乃遣還鎮，令更上捷音。

translations.literal: He then sent him back to his post and ordered him to submit a new report of victory.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent him back to his post and ordered him to submit a new report of victory.

sentences.zh: 守仁乃易前奏，言「奉威武大將軍方略討平叛亂」，而盡入諸嬖幸名，江彬等乃無言。

translations.literal: Shouren then altered his former memorial, saying he "followed the Grand General of Martial Prestige's strategy in pacifying the rebellion," and entered the names of all the favored minions; Jiang Bin and the rest then had nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren then altered his former memorial, saying he had followed the Grand General of Martial Prestige's strategy in pacifying the rebellion, and entered the names of all the favorites; Jiang Bin and the rest then had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 當是時，讒邪構煽，禍變叵測，微守仁，東南事幾殆。

translations.literal: At that time slanderers and the wicked stirred trouble; calamity and change were hard to foresee; but for Shouren, affairs in the southeast would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time slanderers and the wicked were stirring trouble and disaster was hard to foresee; but for Shouren, the southeast would nearly have been lost.

sentences.zh: 世宗深知之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong understood this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong understood this well.

sentences.zh: 甫即位 ，趣召入朝受封。

translations.literal: As soon as he took the throne he urgently summoned Shouren to court to receive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took the throne he urgently summoned Shouren to court to receive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 而大學士楊廷和與王瓊不相能。

translations.literal: But Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and Wang Qiong did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: But Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and Wang Qiong were at odds.

sentences.zh: 守仁前後平賊，率歸功瓊，廷和不喜，大臣亦多忌其功。

translations.literal: In pacifying bandits before and after, Shouren had consistently attributed merit to Qiong; Tinghe was displeased, and many great ministers also resented his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In his campaigns against bandits Shouren had consistently given the credit to Qiong; Tinghe was displeased, and many ministers also resented his achievements.

sentences.zh: 會有言國哀未畢，不宜舉宴行賞者，因拜守仁南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: It happened that some said national mourning was not yet complete and it was improper to hold feasts and grant rewards; Shouren was therefore appointed Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that national mourning was not yet complete and it was improper to hold feasts and grant rewards; Shouren was therefore appointed Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 守仁不赴，請歸省。

translations.literal: Shouren did not take up the post and asked to return home to visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren did not take up the post and asked to return home to visit his parents.

sentences.zh: 已，論功封特進光祿大夫、柱國、新建伯，世襲，歲祿一千石。

translations.literal: Later, in assessing merit he was enfeoffed as specially promoted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Earl of Xinjian, with hereditary succession and an annual stipend of one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when merit was assessed, he was enfeoffed as specially promoted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Earl of Xinjian, with hereditary succession and an annual stipend of one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 然不予鐵券，歲祿亦不給。

translations.literal: Yet he was not granted an iron certificate, nor was the annual stipend paid.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was not granted an iron certificate, nor was his annual stipend paid.

sentences.zh: 諸同事有功者，惟吉安守伍文定至大官，當上賞。

translations.literal: Of his colleagues who had merit, only the Ji'an prefect Wu Wendading rose to a high post and deserved the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who had served with merit, only Ji'an Prefect Wu Wendading rose to high office and deserved the highest reward.

sentences.zh: 其他皆名示遷，而陰絀之，廢斥無存者。

translations.literal: The rest were nominally shown promotions while secretly demoted; dismissed and cast out, none remained.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were nominally promoted while secretly demoted; dismissed and cast out, none remained in office.

sentences.zh: 守仁憤甚。

translations.literal: Shouren was deeply angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was furious.

sentences.zh: 時已丁父憂，屢疏辭爵，乞錄諸臣功，咸報寢。

translations.literal: He was then in mourning for his father; he repeatedly memorialized to decline the enfeoffment and begged that the merit of the various officials be recorded—all were reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He was then in mourning for his father; he repeatedly memorialized to decline the title and begged that his colleagues' merit be recorded—all were shelved.

sentences.zh: 免喪，亦不召。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was still not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was still not summoned.

sentences.zh: 久之，所善席書及門人方獻夫、黃綰以議禮得幸，言於張璁、桂萼，將召用，而費宏故銜守仁，復沮之。

translations.literal: After a long time, his friends Xi Shu and his disciples Fang Xianfu and Huang Guan, who had gained favor through the Rites Controversy, spoke to Zhang Cong and Gui E about summoning him, but Fei Hong bore an old grudge against Shouren and again obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time his friends Xi Shu and his disciples Fang Xianfu and Huang Guan, who had gained favor in the Rites Controversy, spoke to Zhang Cong and Gui E about summoning him, but Fei Hong bore an old grudge against Shouren and blocked it again.

sentences.zh: 屢推兵部尚書，三邊總督，提督團營，皆弗果用。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recommended for Minister of War, grand coordinator of the three frontiers, and supervisor of the regiment camps, but none came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly recommended for Minister of War, grand coordinator of the three frontiers, and supervisor of the regiment camps, but none came to pass.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，思恩、田州土酋盧蘇、王受反。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing the native chieftains of Si'en and Tianzhou, Lu Su and Wang Shou, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6 (1527) the native chieftains of Si'en and Tianzhou, Lu Su and Wang Shou, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 總督姚鏌不能定，乃詔守仁以原官兼左都御史，總督兩廣兼巡撫。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Yao Mo could not pacify them; the emperor then ordered Shouren, in his former rank plus Left Censor-in-Chief, to be grand coordinator of the two Guang and also grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yao Mo could not pacify them; the emperor then ordered Shouren, retaining his former rank plus Left Censor-in-Chief, to be grand coordinator of the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 綰因上書訟守仁功，請賜鐵券、歲祿 ，並敘討賊諸臣，帝咸報可。

translations.literal: Guan thereupon memorialized in defense of Shouren's merit, asking that an iron certificate and annual stipend be granted and that the officials who suppressed the bandits be recorded; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Guan thereupon memorialized in defense of Shouren's merit, asking for an iron certificate and annual stipend and that the officials who suppressed the rebels be rewarded; the emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 守仁在道，疏陳用兵之非，且言：「思恩未設流官，土酋歲出兵三千，聽官征調。

translations.literal: Shouren, on the road, memorialized that military action was wrong and said: "Before Si'en had a regular official, the native chieftain each year sent out three thousand troops at the government's call.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Shouren memorialized that war was wrong and said: "Before Si'en had a regular official, the native chieftain each year sent three thousand troops at the government's call.

sentences.zh: 既設流官，我反歲遣兵數千防戍。

translations.literal: Once a regular official was set up, we instead each year sent several thousand troops to garrison and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once a regular official was installed, we instead had to send several thousand troops each year to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 是流官之設，無益可知。

translations.literal: That setting up regular officials is of no benefit is thus clear.
translations.idiomatic: It is clear that installing regular officials brought no benefit.

sentences.zh: 且田州鄰交阯，深山絕谷，悉瑤、僮盤據，必仍設土官，斯可藉其兵力為屏蔽。

translations.literal: Moreover Tianzhou borders Jiaozhi; deep mountains and sheer valleys are all occupied by Yao and Zhuang; native officials must still be set up so their military strength can serve as a screen.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Tianzhou borders Jiaozhi; deep mountains and sheer valleys are held by Yao and Zhuang; native officials must remain in place so their troops can serve as a screen.

sentences.zh: 若改土為流，則邊鄙之患，我自當之，後必有悔。」

translations.literal: If native rule is changed to regular administration, border troubles we must bear ourselves, and later there will surely be regret.
translations.idiomatic: If native rule is replaced with regular administration, we ourselves must bear the border troubles, and later we will surely regret it.

sentences.zh: 章下兵部，尚書王時中條其不合者五，帝令守仁更議。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Ministry of War; Minister Wang Shizhong listed five points where it did not accord; the emperor ordered Shouren to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of War; Minister Wang Shizhong listed five objections; the emperor ordered Shouren to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 十二月，守仁抵潯州，會巡按御史石金定計招撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Shouren reached Xunzhou and met the touring censor Shi Jin to plan pacification by appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shouren reached Xunzhou and met Touring Censor Shi Jin to plan a policy of appeasement.

sentences.zh: 悉散遣諸軍，留永順、保靖土兵數千，解甲休息。

translations.literal: He dismissed all the armies, retaining several thousand native troops of Yongshun and Baojing, who laid down arms and rested.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed all the armies, retaining only several thousand native troops from Yongshun and Baojing, who laid down arms and rested.

sentences.zh: 蘇、受初求撫不得，聞守仁至益懼，至是則大喜。

translations.literal: Su and Shou at first sought appeasement without success; hearing Shouren was coming they grew still more afraid, but now were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Shou had first sought appeasement without success; hearing Shouren was coming they had grown more afraid, but now were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 守仁赴南寧，二人遣使乞降，守仁令詣軍門。

translations.literal: Shouren went to Nanning; the two sent envoys begging to surrender; Shouren ordered them to come to army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren went to Nanning; the two sent envoys to beg surrender; Shouren ordered them to come to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二人竊議曰：「王公素多詐，恐紿我。」

translations.literal: The two whispered among themselves: "Lord Wang has always been full of stratagems; he may be deceiving us.
translations.idiomatic: The two whispered: "Lord Wang has always been full of tricks; he may be deceiving us.

sentences.zh: 陳兵入見。

translations.literal: They arrayed troops and entered to see him.
translations.idiomatic: They came in with troops arrayed.

sentences.zh: 守仁數二人罪，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: Shouren recounted the two men's crimes, beat them, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren recounted their crimes, had them beaten, and released them.

sentences.zh: 親入營，撫其眾七萬。

translations.literal: He personally entered the camp and reassured their host of seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He personally entered the camp and reassured their host of seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 奏聞於朝，陳用兵十害，招撫十善。

translations.literal: He reported to court, setting forth ten harms of using troops and ten benefits of appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to court, setting forth ten harms of war and ten benefits of appeasement.

sentences.zh: 因請復設流官，量割田州地，別立一州，以岑猛次子邦相為吏目，署州事，俟有功擢知州。

translations.literal: He then asked to restore a regular official, measure out and cut off Tianzhou territory to establish a separate prefecture, appoint Cen Meng's second son Bangxiang as clerk to administer prefectural affairs, and promote him to magistrate when he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to restore a regular official, carve out part of Tianzhou to establish a separate prefecture, appoint Cen Meng's second son Bangxiang as clerk to administer it, and promote him to magistrate when he earned merit.

sentences.zh: 而於田州置十九巡檢司，以蘇、受等任之，並受約束於流官知府。

translations.literal: In Tianzhou he set up nineteen inspection offices, with Su, Shou, and others appointed to them, all subject to the regular prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzhou he set up nineteen inspection offices staffed by Su, Shou, and others, all subject to the regular prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 斷藤峽瑤賊，上連八寨，下通仙台、花相諸洞蠻，盤亙三百余里，郡邑罹害者數十年。

translations.literal: The Yao bandits of Duanteng Gorge linked above with the Eight Stockades and below with the cave tribes of Xiantai, Huaxiang, and others, sprawling over more than three hundred li; prefectures and counties had suffered for decades.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao bandits of Duanteng Gorge linked above with the Eight Stockades and below with the cave tribes of Xiantai and Huaxiang, sprawling over more than three hundred li; prefectures and counties had suffered for decades.

sentences.zh: 守仁欲討之，故留南寧。

translations.literal: Shouren wished to campaign against them and therefore remained at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren wished to campaign against them and therefore remained at Nanning.

sentences.zh: 罷湖廣兵，示不再用。

translations.literal: He dismissed the Huguang troops, showing they would not be used again.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the Huguang troops to show they would not be used again.

sentences.zh: 伺賊不備，進破牛腸、六寺等十余寨，峽賊悉平。

translations.literal: Waiting until the bandits were unprepared, he advanced and broke more than ten stockades including Niuchang and Liusi; the gorge bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting until the bandits were off guard, he advanced and broke more than ten stockades including Niuchang and Liusi; the gorge bandits were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 遂循橫石江而下，攻克仙台、花相、白竹、古陶、羅鳳諸賊。

translations.literal: He then followed the Hengshi River downstream and took the bandits of Xiantai, Huaxiang, Baizhu, Gutao, Luofeng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the Hengshi River downstream and took the bandits of Xiantai, Huaxiang, Baizhu, Gutao, Luofeng, and others.

sentences.zh: 令布政使林富率蘇、受兵直抵八寨，破石門，副將沈希儀邀斬軼賊，盡平八寨。

translations.literal: He ordered the provincial administration commissioner Lin Fu to lead Su and Shou's troops straight to the Eight Stockades, break Shimen, and with Vice General Shen Xiyi intercept and kill fleeing bandits, pacifying all eight stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Lin Fu to lead Su and Shou's troops straight to the Eight Stockades, break Shimen, and with Vice General Shen Xiyi intercept and kill fleeing bandits, pacifying all eight stockades.

sentences.zh: 始，帝以蘇、受之撫，遣行人奉璽書獎諭。

translations.literal: At first, because of the appeasement of Su and Shou, the emperor sent an emissary bearing an imperial seal letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Su and Shou had submitted, the emperor sent an emissary with an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 及奏斷藤峽捷，則以手詔問閣臣楊一清等，謂守仁自誇大 ，且及其生平學術。

translations.literal: When victory at Duanteng Gorge was reported, he used a handwritten edict to ask the grand secretary Yang Yiqing and others whether Shouren was boasting, and also touched on his lifelong learning.
translations.idiomatic: When victory at Duanteng Gorge was reported, he used a handwritten edict to ask Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and others whether Shouren was boasting, and also touched on his philosophy.

sentences.zh: 一清等不知所對。

translations.literal: Yiqing and the others did not know how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing and the others did not know how to reply.

sentences.zh: 守仁之起由璁、萼薦，萼故不善守仁，以璁強之。

translations.literal: Shouren's rise came through recommendation by Cong and E; E had never favored Shouren and was pressed by Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren's recall came through recommendation by Cong and E; E had never liked Shouren and was pressed by Cong.

sentences.zh: 後萼長吏部，璁入內閣，積不相下。

translations.literal: Later E headed the Ministry of Personnel and Cong entered the Grand Secretariat; they were long at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Later E headed the Ministry of Personnel and Cong entered the Grand Secretariat; they were long at odds.

sentences.zh: 萼暴貴喜功名，風守仁取交阯，守仁辭不應。

translations.literal: E rose suddenly to wealth and loved achievement and fame; he urged Shouren to take Jiaozhi; Shouren declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: E rose suddenly and loved glory; he urged Shouren to take Jiaozhi; Shouren declined.

sentences.zh: 一清雅知守仁，而黃綰嘗上疏欲令守仁入輔，毀一清，一清亦不能無移憾。

translations.literal: Yiqing truly understood Shouren, but Huang Guan had once memorialized wishing Shouren to enter as assistant minister and slandered Yiqing; Yiqing also could not be without a shift of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing truly valued Shouren, but Huang Guan had once memorialized for Shouren to enter the cabinet and slandered Yiqing; Yiqing too could not help resenting it.

sentences.zh: 萼遂顯詆守仁征撫交失，賞格不行。

translations.literal: E then openly slandered Shouren for failures in campaigning and appeasement in Jiaozhi, and rewards were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: E then openly attacked Shouren for failures in the Guang campaigns and blocked the promised rewards.

sentences.zh: 獻夫及霍韜不平，上疏爭之，言：「諸瑤為患積年，初嘗用兵數十萬，僅得一田州，旋復召寇。

translations.literal: Xianfu and Huo Tao were indignant and memorialized in protest, saying: "The various Yao had been a scourge for years; at first several hundred thousand troops were used and only Tianzhou was gained, then bandits were summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu and Huo Tao were indignant and memorialized in protest, saying: "The Yao had plagued the region for years; at first several hundred thousand troops were used and only Tianzhou was gained, then the troubles returned.

sentences.zh: 守仁片言馳諭，思、田稽首。

translations.literal: Shouren with a few words sent in haste admonished them, and Si'en and Tianzhou bowed their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren with a few swift words brought them to submit, and Si'en and Tianzhou bowed their heads.

sentences.zh: 至八寨、斷藤峽賊，阻深岩絕岡，國初以來未有輕議剿者，今一舉蕩平，若拉枯朽。

translations.literal: As for the bandits of the Eight Stockades and Duanteng Gorge, blocked by deep cliffs and sheer ridges, since the founding of the dynasty none had lightly proposed suppression; now in one stroke they were swept away, as if pulling down rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Eight Stockades and Duanteng Gorge bandits, walled in by deep cliffs and sheer ridges, since the founding of the dynasty no one had lightly proposed suppressing them; now in one stroke they were swept away like rotten timber.

sentences.zh: 議者乃言守仁受命征思、田，不受命征八寨。

translations.literal: Critics then said Shouren had received orders to campaign against Si'en and Tianzhou but not orders to campaign against the Eight Stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Critics then said Shouren had orders to campaign against Si'en and Tianzhou but not against the Eight Stockades.

sentences.zh: 夫大夫出疆，有可以安國家，利社稷，專之可也，況守仁固承詔得便宜從事者乎？

translations.literal: When a great officer goes beyond the frontier, if he can secure the state and benefit the altars of soil and grain, he may act on his own authority; how much more so when Shouren had indeed received orders to act with discretionary power?
translations.idiomatic: When a great officer goes beyond the frontier, if he can secure the state and benefit the realm, he may act on his own authority; how much more when Shouren had imperial orders to act at discretion?

sentences.zh: 守仁討平叛籓，忌者誣以初同賊謀，又誣其輦載金帛。

translations.literal: Shouren suppressed the rebel princely establishment; the jealous slandered him as having first conspired with the rebels and also slandered him for loading carts with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren had put down the rebel prince; the jealous slandered him as having first conspired with the rebels and as having loaded carts with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 當時大臣楊廷和、喬宇飾成其事，至今未白。

translations.literal: The great ministers of the time, Yang Tinghe and Qiao Yu, embellished and completed this affair; to this day it has not been cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers Yang Tinghe and Qiao Yu had helped make this slander stick; to this day it has not been cleared.

sentences.zh: 夫忠如守仁，有功如守仁，一屈於江西，再屈於兩廣。
