translations.literal: Loyal as Shouren, meritorious as Shouren—once humbled in Jiangxi, again humbled in the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal as Shouren, meritorious as Shouren—once humbled in Jiangxi, again humbled in the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 臣恐勞臣灰心，將士解體，後此疆圉有事，誰復為陛下任之！」

translations.literal: Your servant fears that laboring ministers will lose heart and officers and soldiers will dissolve; hereafter if the frontier has trouble, who will again bear it for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: I fear that loyal servants will lose heart and troops will lose spirit; hereafter if the frontier has trouble, who will bear it for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 帝報聞而已。

translations.literal: The emperor merely acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor merely acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 守仁已病甚，疏乞骸骨，舉鄖陽巡撫林富自代，不俟命竟歸。

translations.literal: Shouren was already gravely ill; he memorialized begging to retire, recommended the Yunyang grand coordinator Lin Fu to replace him, and returned without awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was already gravely ill; he memorialized to retire, recommended Yunyang Grand Coordinator Lin Fu to replace him, and returned without awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 行至南安卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: When he reached Nan'an he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nan'an he died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 喪過江西 ，軍民無不縞素哭送者。

translations.literal: As the funeral procession passed through Jiangxi, soldiers and civilians none failed to wear mourning white and weep as they sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession passed through Jiangxi, soldiers and civilians alike wore mourning white and wept as they sent him off.

sentences.zh: 守仁天姿異敏。

translations.literal: Shouren's natural endowment was exceptionally keen.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was exceptionally quick of mind.

sentences.zh: 年十七謁上饒婁諒，與論硃子格物大指。

translations.literal: At seventeen he visited Lou Liang of Shangrao and discussed with him the main points of Zhu Xi's investigation of things.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he visited Lou Liang of Shangrao and discussed Zhu Xi's doctrine of investigating things.

sentences.zh: 還家，日端坐，講讀《五經》，不苟言笑。

translations.literal: Returning home, he sat upright each day, lecturing on and reading the Five Classics, not casual in speech or laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he sat upright each day lecturing on the Five Classics, never casual in speech or laughter.

sentences.zh: 游九華歸 ，築室陽明洞中。

translations.literal: After traveling to Jiuhua he returned and built a dwelling in Yangming Cave.
translations.idiomatic: After traveling to Jiuhua he returned and built a dwelling in Yangming Cave.

sentences.zh: 泛濫二氏學，數年無所得。

translations.literal: He drifted broadly through the learning of the two schools, Daoist and Buddhist, and for several years gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He drifted through Daoist and Buddhist learning for several years and gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 謫龍場，窮荒無書，日繹舊聞。

translations.literal: Banished to Longchang, in remote wilderness without books, he daily unraveled what he had heard before.
translations.idiomatic: Banished to Longchang, in remote wilderness without books, he daily turned over what he had learned before.

sentences.zh: 忽悟格物致知，當自求諸心，不當求諸事物，喟然曰：「道在是矣。」

translations.literal: Suddenly he understood that investigating things and extending knowledge must be sought in the mind, not sought in things, and sighed: "The Way is here.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he understood that investigating things and extending knowledge must be sought in the mind, not in external things, and sighed: "The Way is here.

sentences.zh: 遂篤信不疑。

translations.literal: Thereafter he believed firmly without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he believed it firmly.

sentences.zh: 其為教，專以致良知為主。

translations.literal: In his teaching he focused solely on extending innate knowing.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching he focused solely on extending innate knowing.

sentences.zh: 謂宋周、程二子後，惟象山陸氏簡易直捷，有以接孟氏之傳。

translations.literal: He held that after the Song masters Zhou and the two Chengs, only Xiangshan Lu's school was simple, direct, and swift, and could link to Mencius's transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He held that after the Song masters Zhou and the two Chengs, only Xiangshan Lu's school was simple and direct enough to link to Mencius's transmission.

sentences.zh: 而硃子《集注》、《或問》之類，乃中年未定之說。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries, Or Questions, and the like were doctrines of his middle years not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries, Or Questions, and the like were doctrines of his middle years, not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 學者翕然從之，世遂有「陽明學」雲。

translations.literal: Scholars flocked to follow him, and the age came to have what was called "Yangming learning."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars flocked to follow him, and the age came to speak of Yangming learning.

sentences.zh: 守仁既卒，桂萼奏其擅離職守。

translations.literal: After Shouren died, Gui E memorialized that he had left his post without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouren died, Gui E memorialized that he had left his post without authorization.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered court ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered the court to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 萼等言：「守仁事不師古，言不稱師。

translations.literal: E and others said: "Shouren in affairs does not take antiquity as teacher; in speech he does not call anyone teacher.
translations.idiomatic: E and others said: "Shouren in affairs does not follow antiquity; in speech he does not honor teachers.

sentences.zh: 欲立異以為高，則非硃熹格物致知之論；

translations.literal: Wishing to set up heterodoxy to make himself lofty, he rejects Zhu Xi's doctrine of investigating things and extending knowledge;
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to set up heterodoxy to make himself lofty, he rejects Zhu Xi's doctrine of investigating things and extending knowledge;

sentences.zh: 知眾論之不予 ，則為硃熹晚年定論之書。

translations.literal: knowing public opinion would not grant it, he produces books of Zhu Xi's settled conclusions in his later years.
translations.idiomatic: knowing public opinion would not accept it, he claims Zhu Xi's later settled conclusions.

sentences.zh: 號召門徒，互相倡和。

translations.literal: He calls disciples and they echo one another.
translations.idiomatic: He calls disciples and they echo one another.

sentences.zh: 才美者樂其任意，庸鄙者借其虛聲。

translations.literal: The talented delight in his wilfulness; the mediocre and base borrow his empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The talented delight in his license; the mediocre borrow his empty fame.

sentences.zh: 傳習轉訛，背謬彌甚。

translations.literal: Transmission and practice turn ever more erroneous; departure and error grow ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission and practice grow ever more erroneous; error grows ever greater.

sentences.zh: 但討捕畲賊，擒獲叛籓，功有足錄，宜免追奪伯爵以章大信，禁邪說以正人心。」

translations.literal: Yet in suppressing She bandits and capturing the rebel princely establishment his merit is worth recording; the earldom should be spared posthumous confiscation to manifest great faith, and heterodox doctrines forbidden to rectify people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in suppressing She bandits and capturing the rebel prince his merit is worth recording; the earldom should not be posthumously stripped to show imperial faith, and heterodox doctrines should be forbidden to rectify hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔停世襲，恤典俱不行。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict halting hereditary succession; condolence rites were all withheld.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict halting hereditary succession; condolence rites were all withheld.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，廷臣多頌其功。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing many court ministers praised his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing many court ministers praised his merit.

sentences.zh: 詔贈新建侯，諡文成。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinjian with the posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xinjian with the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 二年予世襲伯爵。

translations.literal: In the second year hereditary succession to the earldom was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year hereditary succession to the earldom was granted.

sentences.zh: 既又有請以守仁與薛瑄、陳獻章同從祀文廟者。

translations.literal: Later there was again a request that Shouren, together with Xue Xuan and Chen Xianzhang, be granted secondary sacrifice in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was again a request that Shouren, together with Xue Xuan and Chen Xianzhang, be granted secondary sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 帝獨允禮臣議，以瑄配。

translations.literal: The emperor approved only the rites officials' proposal to enshrine Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved only the rites officials' proposal to enshrine Xuan.

sentences.zh: 及萬曆十二年，御史詹事講申前請。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year of Wanli, Censor Zhan Shijiang renewed the earlier request.
translations.idiomatic: By Wanli 12 (1584), Censor Zhan Shijiang renewed the earlier request.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行等言：「守仁言致知出《大學》 ，良知出《孟子》。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others said: "Shouren's extending knowledge comes from the Great Learning; innate knowing comes from Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others said: "Shouren's extending knowledge comes from the Great Learning; innate knowing comes from Mencius.

sentences.zh: 陳獻章主靜，沿宋儒周敦頤、程顥。

translations.literal: Chen Xianzhang upheld stillness, following the Song Ruists Zhou Dunyi and Cheng Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianzhang upheld stillness, following the Song Ruists Zhou Dunyi and Cheng Hao.

sentences.zh: 且孝友出處如獻章，氣節文章功業如守仁，不可謂禪，誠宜崇祀。」

translations.literal: Moreover in filial piety, brotherly duty, and conduct in office he is like Xianzhang; in integrity, literary works, and achievements he is like Shouren—they cannot be called Chan Buddhism and truly deserve honored sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in filial piety and conduct in office he is like Xianzhang; in integrity, literary works, and achievements he is like Shouren—they cannot be called Chan Buddhism and truly deserve honored sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 且言胡居仁純心篤行，眾論所歸，亦宜並祀。

translations.literal: They also said Hu Juren had a pure heart and sincere conduct to which public opinion inclined, and he too should be enshrined together.
translations.idiomatic: They also said Hu Juren had a pure heart and sincere conduct to which public opinion inclined, and he too should be enshrined.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，從祀者止守仁等四人。

translations.literal: Through the entire Ming, those granted secondary sacrifice were only Shouren and three others.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Ming, only Shouren and three others were granted secondary sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 始守仁無子，育弟子正憲為後。

translations.literal: At first Shouren had no son and raised his disciple Zhengxian as heir.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shouren had no son and raised his disciple Zhengxian as heir.

sentences.zh: 晚年，生子正億，二歲而孤。

translations.literal: In his later years he had a son Zhengyi, who was orphaned at two.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he had a son Zhengyi, who was orphaned at two.

sentences.zh: 既長，襲錦衣副千戶。

translations.literal: When grown he inherited the deputy thousand-household post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he inherited the deputy thousand-household post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初 ，襲新建伯。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he inherited the earldom of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he inherited the earldom of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wanli 5 (1577).

sentences.zh: 子承勛嗣，督漕運二十年。

translations.literal: His son Chengxun succeeded and supervised grain transport for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengxun succeeded and supervised grain transport for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 子先進，無子，將以弟先達子業弘繼。

translations.literal: His son Xianjin had no son; the plan was for his younger brother Xianda's son Yehong to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianjin had no son; the plan was for his younger brother Xianda's son Yehong to succeed.

sentences.zh: 先達妻曰：「伯無子，爵自傳吾夫。

translations.literal: Xianda's wife said: "The elder brother has no son; the title should pass from my husband.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda's wife said: "The elder brother has no son; the title should pass to my husband.

sentences.zh: 由父及子，爵安往？」

translations.literal: From father to son—where would the title go?
translations.idiomatic: From father to son—where would the title go?

sentences.zh: 先進怒，因育族子業洵為後。

translations.literal: Xianjin was angry and therefore raised a clansman's son Yexun as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xianjin was angry and therefore raised a clansman's son Yexun as heir.

sentences.zh: 及承勛卒，先進未襲死。

translations.literal: When Chengxun died, Xianjin had not yet inherited the title when he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengxun died, Xianjin had not yet inherited the title before he too died.

sentences.zh: 業洵自以非嫡嗣，終當歸爵先達，且虞其爭，乃謗先達為乞養，而別推承勛弟子先通當嗣，屢爭於朝，數十年不決。

translations.literal: Yexun, believing himself not the legitimate heir and that the title would ultimately return to Xianda, and fearing a struggle, slandered Xianda as having begged to adopt an heir and instead pushed Chengxun's nephew Xiantong as successor; they disputed repeatedly at court for decades without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Yexun, believing himself not the legitimate heir and that the title would ultimately pass to Xianda, and fearing a contest, slandered Xianda as having begged to adopt an heir and instead pushed Chengxun's nephew Xiantong as successor; the dispute raged at court for decades without resolution.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，先達子業弘復與先通疏辨。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, Xianda's son Yehong again memorialized in dispute with Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen, Xianda's son Yehong again memorialized against Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 而業洵兄業浩時為總督，所司懼忤業浩，竟以先通嗣。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Yexun's elder brother Yehao was then grand coordinator; the officials feared offending Yehao and ultimately made Xiantong the successor.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yexun's elder brother Yehao was then grand coordinator; the officials feared offending him and ultimately awarded succession to Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 業弘憤，持疏入禁門訴。

translations.literal: Yehong was furious and took a memorial into the forbidden gate to plead.
translations.idiomatic: Yehong was furious and took a memorial through the forbidden gate to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 自刎不殊，執下獄，尋釋。

translations.literal: He cut his throat but did not die; he was arrested and imprisoned, and soon released.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his throat but did not die; he was arrested and imprisoned, then soon released.

sentences.zh: 先通襲伯四年，流賊陷京師，被殺。

translations.literal: Xiantong inherited the earldom four years; when roving bandits took the capital he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiantong held the earldom four years; when roving bandits took the capital he was killed.

sentences.zh: 守仁弟子盈天下，其有傳者不覆載。

translations.literal: Shouren's disciples filled the realm; those with transmission are not all recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren's disciples filled the realm; not all who transmitted his teaching are recorded here.

sentences.zh: 惟冀元亨嘗與守仁共患難。

translations.literal: Only Ji Yuanheng once shared hardship with Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ji Yuanheng once shared hardship with Shouren.

sentences.zh: 附 冀元亨

translations.literal: Appendix: Ji Yuanheng
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Ji Yuanheng

sentences.zh: 冀元亨，字惟乾，武陵人。

translations.literal: Ji Yuanheng, courtesy name Weiqian, was a native of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Yuanheng, whose courtesy name was Weiqian, came from Wuling.

sentences.zh: 篤信守仁學。

translations.literal: He devotedly upheld Shouren's learning.
translations.idiomatic: He devotedly upheld Shouren's learning.

sentences.zh: 舉正德十一年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the eleventh year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Zhengde 11 (1516).

sentences.zh: 從守仁於贛，守仁屬以教子。

translations.literal: He followed Shouren in Ganzhou; Shouren entrusted him to teach his son.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shouren in Ganzhou, and Shouren entrusted him to teach his son.

sentences.zh: 宸濠懷不軌，而外務名高，貽書守仁問學，守仁使元亨往。

translations.literal: Chen Hao harbored rebellious designs but outwardly pursued lofty reputation; he sent a letter to Shouren asking about learning; Shouren sent Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao harbored rebellious designs but outwardly cultivated a lofty reputation; he wrote Shouren asking about learning, and Shouren sent Yuanheng in reply.

sentences.zh: 宸濠語挑之，佯不喻，獨與之論學，宸濠目為痴。

translations.literal: Chen Hao's words were provocative; Yuanheng feigned not to understand and only discussed learning with him; Chen Hao regarded him as a fool.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao spoke provocatively; Yuanheng pretended not to understand and discussed only learning with him; Chen Hao took him for a fool.

sentences.zh: 他日講《西銘》，反覆君臣義甚悉。

translations.literal: Another day lecturing on the Western Inscription, he repeatedly expounded lord-and-minister righteousness very fully.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, lecturing on the Western Inscription, he expounded lord-and-minister righteousness again and again with great fullness.

sentences.zh: 宸濠亦服，厚贈遣之，元亨反其贈於官。

translations.literal: Chen Hao also submitted; he gave lavish gifts to send him off; Yuanheng returned the gifts to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao was won over as well; he gave lavish parting gifts, which Yuanheng turned over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 已，宸濠敗，張忠、許泰誣守仁與通。

translations.literal: Later when Chen Hao was defeated, Zhang Zhong and Xu Tai slandered Shouren as having communicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chen Hao was defeated, Zhang Zhong and Xu Tai slandered Shouren as having been in league with him.

sentences.zh: 詰宸濠，言無有。

translations.literal: Interrogating Chen Hao, he said there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Hao was interrogated, he said there was nothing of the kind.

sentences.zh: 忠等詰不已，曰：「獨嘗遣冀元亨論學。」

translations.literal: Zhong and others kept pressing; he said: "I only once sent Ji Yuanheng to discuss learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the others kept pressing him; he said: "I only once sent Ji Yuanheng to discuss learning.

sentences.zh: 忠等大喜，搒元亨，加以砲烙，終不承，械系京師詔獄。

translations.literal: Zhong and others were greatly pleased; they beat Yuanheng and applied branding irons; he still would not confess and was shackled and held in the capital imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and the others were delighted; they beat Yuanheng and applied branding irons; he still would not confess and was shackled in the capital imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，言者交白其冤，出獄五日卒。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, memorializers repeatedly cleared his injustice; he left prison and died five days later.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, memorializers repeatedly cleared his name; he left prison and died five days later.

sentences.zh: 元亨在獄，善待諸囚若兄弟，囚皆感泣。

translations.literal: In prison Yuanheng treated all prisoners kindly as brothers; the prisoners all wept with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: In prison Yuanheng treated the other prisoners like brothers; they all wept at his kindness.

sentences.zh: 其被逮也，所司系其妻李，李無怖色，曰：「吾夫尊師樂善，豈他慮哉！」

translations.literal: When he was arrested, the authorities also imprisoned his wife Li; Li showed no fear and said: "My husband honors his teacher and delights in goodness—what else is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: When he was arrested, the authorities imprisoned his wife Li as well; Li showed no fear and said: "My husband honors his teacher and delights in doing good—what else should I worry about?

sentences.zh: 獄中與二女治麻枲不輟。

translations.literal: In prison she and her two daughters worked hemp and ramie without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In prison she and her two daughters worked hemp and ramie without pause.

sentences.zh: 事且白，守者欲出之。

translations.literal: When the affair was about to be cleared, the keepers wished to release her.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was about to be cleared, the keepers wished to release her.

sentences.zh: 曰：「未見吾夫，出安往？」

translations.literal: She said: "I have not yet seen my husband—where would I go?
translations.idiomatic: She said: "I have not yet seen my husband—where would I go?

sentences.zh: 按察諸僚婦聞其賢，召之，辭不赴。

translations.literal: The wives of colleagues in the surveillance commission, hearing of her worth, summoned her; she declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: The wives of surveillance officials, hearing of her virtue, summoned her; she declined to go.

sentences.zh: 已就見，則囚服見，手不釋麻枲。

translations.literal: When she did go to see them, she wore prisoner's garb and did not lay down the hemp and ramie from her hands.
translations.idiomatic: When she did go, she came in prisoner's garb and did not lay down the hemp and ramie in her hands.

sentences.zh: 問其夫學，曰：「吾夫之學，不出閨門衽席間。」

translations.literal: Asked about her husband's learning, she said: "My husband's learning does not go beyond the women's quarters and bed mats.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about her husband's learning, she said: "My husband's learning does not go beyond the women's quarters and the bed mats.

sentences.zh: 聞者悚然。

translations.literal: Those who heard were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were startled.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王守仁始以直節著。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Wang Shouren at first was known for upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Wang Shouren at first was known for upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 比任疆事，提弱卒，從諸書生掃積年逋寇，平定孽籓。

translations.literal: When he took frontier duty, he led weak troops with various scholars to sweep away bandits accumulated over years and pacify the rebellious princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When he took frontier duty, he led weak troops alongside scholars to sweep away bandits of many years' standing and pacify the rebel prince.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，文臣用兵制勝，未有如守仁者也。

translations.literal: Through the entire Ming, among civil officials using troops to achieve victory, none were like Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Ming, no civil official who took the field and won was Shouren's equal.

sentences.zh: 當危疑之際，神明愈定，智慮無遺，雖由天資高，其亦有得於中者歟。

translations.literal: In moments of peril and doubt his spirit grew steadier and his plans left nothing out; though this was due to lofty natural endowment, did he not also gain something within?
translations.idiomatic: In moments of peril and doubt his spirit grew steadier and his plans left nothing out; though this owed much to lofty natural gifts, had he not also gained something within?

sentences.zh: 矜其創獲，標異儒先，卒為學者譏。

translations.literal: He prized his own discoveries and marked himself off from earlier Confucians, and in the end was mocked by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He prized his own discoveries and set himself apart from earlier Confucians, and in the end was mocked by scholars.

sentences.zh: 守仁嘗謂胡世寧少講學，世寧曰：「某恨公多講學耳。」

translations.literal: Shouren once said Hu Shining spoke too little of learning; Shining replied: "I regret that you speak too much of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren once said Hu Shining spoke too little of learning; Shining replied: "I only regret that you speak too much of it.

sentences.zh: 桂萼之議雖出於媢忌之私，抑流弊實然，固不能以功多為諱矣。

translations.literal: Gui E's critique, though born of jealous private motive, also checked real abuses in the stream of learning; one cannot because of great merit cover this up entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E's critique, though born of jealous private motive, also checked real abuses in the school; one cannot, because of great merit, cover that up entirely.
